title: 4-way Bluetooth tower speaker with 8 inch subwoofer

project.prompt: craete a jbl 4way speaker with one sub with bluetooth module

brief.title: 4-way Bluetooth speaker with subwoofer (JBL-style)
brief.understanding: You want to build a large JBL-style Bluetooth speaker that plays music from a phone and splits the sound across four driver sizes, with one subwoofer for deep bass. I have assumed a single mains-powered cabinet in which the subwoofer is the lowest of the four bands (sub, woofer, midrange, tweeter). This is a home-built speaker in that style, not a copy of a JBL product or its branding.

questions.question: What does "4-way with one sub" mean for you?
options: One box: sub + woofer + mid + tweeter
One box: 4 drivers plus a separate sub
Stereo pair of speakers + one sub box
questions.assumed: One box: sub + woofer + mid + tweeter
questions.why: It sets the number of drivers, amplifier channels and cabinets, and so most of the cost.

questions.question: How should it be powered?
questions.why: A battery adds a 6-cell pack, protection and a charger, and limits how loud it can go.

questions.question: How big and loud should it be?
questions.why: Sub size sets the cabinet volume, amplifier and power supply rating.

questions.question: How should the sound be split between the drivers?
options: Simple: passive crossover parts, no programming
Advanced: DSP board (ADAU1701), tunable on a PC
questions.assumed: Simple: passive crossover parts, no programming
questions.why: DSP sounds better and is tunable, but needs four amplifier channels and software setup.

questions.question: What is your budget for parts, including the wood for the box?
questions.why: Driver quality is the largest cost and the largest factor in how it sounds.

requirements: Bluetooth 5.0 audio from a phone (SBC/AAC), range at least 10 m in open space
Four bands in one cabinet: sub below about 120 Hz, woofer 120-800 Hz, midrange 800 Hz-4 kHz, tweeter above 4 kHz
Amplifier power: about 100 W into the 4 ohm subwoofer, plus 2 x 50 W for the upper drivers
Supply: 24 V DC, 6 A (about 150 W) mains adapter with a barrel jack on the rear panel
Frequency response target: 45 Hz to 20 kHz
Controls: power switch, master volume knob, sub level knob; pairing is handled by the Bluetooth module
Cabinet: 18 mm MDF, about 25-30 litres for the sub chamber, with a sealed separate chamber for the midrange; overall about 30 x 35 x 70 cm
Parts cost for one unit of $150-300 including wood

blocks.name: Power input
blocks.role: Converts wall power to 24 V DC for the amplifier and feeds a small regulator for the Bluetooth module.
blocks.parts: 24 V 6 A desktop adapter (Mean Well GST160A24 class), DC jack, rocker switch, LM2596 buck module to 5 V

blocks.name: Bluetooth receiver
blocks.role: Receives music from the phone and outputs a stereo line-level signal.
blocks.parts: Bluetooth 5.0 audio receiver board with line out (QCC3008 or MH-M28 class)

blocks.name: Mono mix and controls
blocks.role: Sums left and right into one signal with two resistors and sets master volume.
blocks.parts: 2 x 4.7k resistors, 10k log potentiometer, ground-loop isolating 5 V supply (B0505S) if hum appears

blocks.name: 2.1 amplifier
blocks.role: Low-pass filters and amplifies the sub channel (100 W) and amplifies two full-range channels (2 x 50 W).
blocks.parts: TPA3116D2 2.1 amplifier board (XH-M139 class) with a sub level/frequency knob

blocks.name: Passive crossover
blocks.role: Splits the two amplifier channels: one drives the woofer, the other drives the midrange and tweeter, each through its filter.
blocks.parts: Air-core/ferrite inductors and polypropylene film capacitors (12 dB/octave), or a ready-made 3-way crossover board at 80

blocks.name: Drivers
blocks.role: Turn the amplified signal into sound across the four bands.
blocks.parts: 8" 4 ohm 100 W subwoofer, 5.25" 4-8 ohm woofer, 3" midrange, 1" dome tweeter (Dayton Audio, or JBL replacement drivers)

blocks.name: Cabinet
blocks.role: Holds the drivers and provides the tuned air volume the subwoofer needs.
blocks.parts: 18 mm MDF, bass-reflex port tube, damping wadding, speaker terminal wire, rear panel for jack, switch and knobs

risks: Hum or whine when the Bluetooth module shares the amplifier supply: power the module through an isolated 5 V converter and keep signal wires short and shielded.

Crossover does not match the chosen drivers (harsh or missing midrange): pick the drivers first, then calculate the crossover from their real impedance and sensitivity, and add a resistor pad to the tweeter if it is too loud.
Weak or boomy bass from wrong cabinet volume or port length: use the sub's Thiele-Small parameters in a free calculator (WinISD) before cutting wood.
Amplifier overheating or shutting down at high volume: do not go below 4 ohm per channel, leave airflow around the heatsink, and check that the supply can deliver 6 A.

answers.crossover: Advanced: DSP board (ADAU1701), tunable on a PC

zones.name: Four drivers on the front baffle
Rear control plate: Bluetooth, mixer and 2.1 amplifier
Rear power plate: DC jack, switch, fuse and 5 V buck

product.name: 4-way Bluetooth tower speaker with 8 inch subwoofer
product.summary: One 18 mm MDF tower, 300 x 350 x 700 mm, with a ported sub chamber of about 26 litres below a fixed shelf and a sealed upper chamber for the woofer, a sealed midrange pocket, the tweeter and the electronics. An external 24 V 6 A desktop adapter feeds a rear barrel jack; a TPA3116D2 2.1 amplifier board drives the sub directly and the upper three drivers through a passive crossover, with a Bluetooth 5.0 receiver board on a 5 V buck rail. It follows the parts blocks in the brief, so it uses an 8 inch sub and a passive crossover; a 10-12 inch sub does not fit the 264 mm internal width and the ADAU1701 DSP is left out. Scale reference: 18 mm MDF panels and the 210 mm frame of the 8 inch driver. Every part is assumed.
product.powerInput: 24 V DC, 6 A (about 150 W) from an external mains desktop adapter, Mean Well GST160A24 class, 5.5 x 2.5 mm barrel jack on the rear panel

parts.name: Front baffle, 18 mm MDF
parts.function: Carries all four drivers and closes the front of both chambers.
parts.material: 18 mm MDF, black textured paint or vinyl wrap
parts.process: CNC routed sheet, glued butt joints
parts.evidence: Brief: 18 mm MDF, front at -Y. Round through-holes on X = 0: 182 mm at Z = -170 (sub), 120 mm at Z = +75 (woofer), 74 mm at Z = +195 (midrange), 45 mm at Z = +285 (tweeter). Drawn as a solid panel; the driver flanges cover the holes. Feet take 12 mm of the 700 mm height, so the panel is 688 mm tall.
parts.unknowns: Driver bolt circles are not confirmed; nominal guesses are 4 screws on about 197 mm (sub), 6 on 135 mm (woofer), 4 on 86 mm (midrange) and 4 on 60 mm (tweeter). Take the real values from the driver datasheets before drilling.

parts.name: Rear panel, 18 mm MDF with two plate openings
parts.function: Closes the rear of both chambers and carries the port and the two screw-on electronics plates.
parts.material: 18 mm MDF, black paint or vinyl wrap
parts.process: CNC routed sheet, glued butt joints
parts.evidence: Brief: openings 200 x 140 mm centred at Z = +230 and 200 x 100 mm centred at Z = +80, both on X = 0; 57 mm hole for the port at X = 0, Z = -220. The 220 mm wide plates overlap each opening by 10 mm per side for screws and a gasket.
parts.unknowns: Final plate outline and screw pattern come from the control and power sub-assemblies. The port hole is not drawn in the lower block.

parts.name: Side panel, 18 mm MDF
parts.function: Forms the left and right walls of both chambers.
parts.material: 18 mm MDF, black paint or vinyl wrap
parts.evidence: Brief: 300 mm outer width gives 264 mm internal width; the sides sit between baffle and rear panel, 314 mm deep.

parts.name: Top panel, 18 mm MDF
parts.function: Closes the top of the sealed upper chamber.
parts.evidence: Brief: glued butt-joint box; the panel fits between the sides, baffle and rear.

parts.name: Bottom panel, 18 mm MDF
parts.function: Floor of the sub chamber and mount for the feet.
parts.evidence: Sits at Z = -338 to -320 so the 12 mm feet stay inside the 700 mm overall height.

parts.name: Fixed sealed shelf, 18 mm MDF
parts.function: Separates the ported sub chamber from the sealed upper chamber; its top face at Z = +3 carries the crossover.
parts.evidence: Brief: shelf spans Z = -15 to +3, glued and sealed on all four edges. Sub chamber below is 264 x 314 x 305 mm, about 25.3 litres gross, slightly under the 26 litre target because of the feet.
parts.unknowns: Net volume after driver and port displacement is about 23.5 to 24 litres. Check the 45 Hz tuning with the real driver's T/S parameters.

parts.name: Sealed midrange pocket, 12 mm MDF
parts.function: Isolates the back of the midrange from the woofer's pressure in the upper chamber.
parts.evidence: Brief: about 120 x 100 x 110 mm outside, glued to the back of the baffle behind the 74 mm hole at Z = +195. Five-sided box open towards the baffle, about 0.7 litre inside.
parts.unknowns: Needs a small sealed hole for the midrange wire. Check that the midrange magnet depth fits the 88 mm internal depth.

parts.name: Bass-reflex port tube, 50 mm ID x 150 mm
parts.function: Tunes the sub chamber to about 45 Hz and vents it through the rear panel.
parts.material: ABS or PVC tube with flared flange
parts.process: Injection moulded or cut pipe, glued into the panel
parts.evidence: Brief: 50 mm inner diameter, 150 mm long, through the rear panel at X = 0, Z = -220, pointing inward. A 50 mm x 150 mm port in about 24 litres net works out to roughly 43 to 46 Hz. The inner end is at Y = +25, about 70 mm clear of the sub magnet.
parts.unknowns: Trim the length after an impedance sweep to hit the tuning.

parts.name: Sealed cable pass-through in shelf
parts.function: Passes the sub speaker wire from the upper chamber into the sub chamber without an air leak.
parts.material: Nylon PG7 gland or drilled hole with hot-melt or silicone seal
parts.evidence: Brief asks for a sealed pass-through for the sub wire. Placed in the rear right corner of the shelf, clear of the crossover board and the power plate.

parts.name: Polyester wadding, sub chamber
parts.function: Damps standing waves in the sub chamber.
parts.evidence: Brief: wadding in both chambers. Pad on the chamber floor behind the driver and below the port so the port mouth stays clear.

parts.name: Polyester wadding, upper chamber
parts.function: Damps internal reflections behind the woofer in the sealed upper chamber.
parts.evidence: Brief: wadding in both chambers. Pad stapled under the top panel, clear of the tweeter, control plate and midrange pocket.

parts.name: Rubber foot, 30 mm
parts.function: Decouples the tower from the floor and stops it sliding.
parts.evidence: Brief: four rubber feet. 12 mm tall, screwed into the bottom panel near the corners.

parts.name: 8 inch subwoofer, Dayton Audio DCS205-4
parts.function: Reproduces the bass band below about 120 Hz into the ported lower chamber.
parts.material: Stamped steel basket, treated paper cone, rubber surround, ferrite magnet
parts.evidence: Named in the brief: 8 inch, 4 ohm, about 210 mm frame and 95 mm deep at Z = -170. Modelled with its front at the Y = -175 box limit; in the real build the flange and gasket sit about 5 mm proud of the baffle face.
parts.unknowns: Exact cut-out (about 184 mm) and bolt circle (about 196 mm) should be taken from the Dayton datasheet before routing the baffle.

parts.name: 5.25 inch woofer, Dayton Audio DC130A-8
parts.function: Reproduces the band from the sub handover up to about 800 Hz in the sealed upper chamber.
parts.material: Stamped steel basket, coated paper cone, rubber surround, ferrite magnet
parts.evidence: Named in the brief: 5.25 inch, 8 ohm, about 150 mm frame and 70 mm deep at Z = +75. Frame drawn at 148 mm so it clears the midrange flange.
parts.unknowns: Exact cut-out (about 124 mm) and bolt circle (about 136 mm) from the datasheet.

parts.name: 3 inch midrange, Dayton Audio PC83-4
parts.function: Reproduces the 800 Hz to 4 kHz band from its own sealed pocket.
parts.material: Stamped steel basket, poly-coated paper cone, rubber surround, ferrite magnet
parts.evidence: Named in the brief: 3 inch, 4 ohm, about 93 mm frame and 55 mm deep at Z = +195. Frame drawn at 92 mm so it clears the woofer flange.
parts.unknowns: Exact cut-out (about 76 mm) and bolt circle (about 84 mm) from the datasheet.

parts.name: 1 inch dome tweeter, Dayton Audio ND25FA-4
parts.function: Reproduces the band above about 4 kHz.
parts.material: Moulded plastic faceplate, silk dome, neodymium magnet
parts.evidence: Named in the brief: 1 inch dome, 4 ohm, about 54 mm faceplate at Z = +285. Depth of 25 mm is typical for a small neodymium tweeter.
parts.unknowns: The stock faceplate hole count may differ from the four screws in the brief; check the datasheet, and the cut-out (about 40 mm).

parts.name: Subwoofer foam gasket ring
parts.function: Seals the sub flange to the baffle so the ported chamber does not leak.
parts.material: Closed-cell EVA or PE foam, adhesive backed
parts.evidence: Brief calls for a foam gasket under each driver. It is a ring about 12 mm wide, drawn as a thin disc behind the flange.

parts.name: Woofer foam gasket ring
parts.function: Seals the woofer flange to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief calls for a foam gasket under each driver; it is a ring, drawn as a thin disc.

parts.name: Midrange foam gasket ring
parts.function: Seals the midrange flange to the baffle and its pocket.
parts.evidence: Brief calls for a foam gasket under each driver; it is a ring, drawn as a thin disc.

parts.name: Tweeter foam gasket ring
parts.function: Seals the tweeter faceplate to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief calls for a foam gasket under each driver; it is a ring, drawn as a thin disc.

parts.name: Subwoofer wood screws, 4 x 22 mm black pan head
parts.function: Clamp the sub frame and gasket to the MDF baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief: four black wood screws per driver. Placed on an assumed 196 mm bolt circle at 45 degrees.
parts.unknowns: Bolt circle to be confirmed from the driver datasheet.

parts.name: Woofer wood screws, 3.5 x 18 mm black pan head
parts.function: Clamp the woofer frame and gasket to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief: four black wood screws per driver. Assumed 136 mm bolt circle at 45 degrees.

parts.name: Midrange wood screws, 3.5 x 18 mm black pan head
parts.function: Clamp the midrange frame and gasket to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief: four black wood screws per driver. Assumed 84 mm bolt circle at 45 degrees.

parts.name: Tweeter wood screws, 3.5 x 18 mm black pan head
parts.function: Clamp the tweeter faceplate and gasket to the baffle.
parts.evidence: Brief: four black wood screws per driver. Assumed 44 mm bolt circle at 45 degrees.
parts.unknowns: Stock faceplate hole pattern may need re-drilling for four screws.

parts.name: Subwoofer spade terminals (+ 6.3 mm, - 4.8 mm)
parts.function: Accept the push-on connectors of the sub wire coming straight from the amplifier sub output.
parts.evidence: Brief: spade terminals at the rear of the magnet on each driver.

parts.name: Woofer spade terminals
parts.function: Accept the low-pass feed from the crossover.
parts.evidence: Brief: spade terminals at the rear of the magnet on each driver.

parts.name: Midrange spade terminals
parts.function: Accept the band-pass feed from the crossover.
parts.evidence: Brief: spade terminals at the rear of the magnet on each driver.

parts.name: Tweeter spade terminals
parts.function: Accept the high-pass feed from the crossover.
parts.evidence: Brief: spade terminals at the rear of the magnet on each driver.

parts.name: Rear control plate, 2 mm black anodised aluminium
parts.function: Carries all control electronics on its inner side and closes the upper rear panel opening.
parts.process: Laser cut, countersunk, anodised, laser-etched legends
parts.evidence: Brief: 220 x 160 x 2 mm plate, outer face at Y = +175, centred at Z = +230. Sits in a 2 mm rebate so it is flush with the MDF; needs a 180 x 120 mm through-opening behind it (X +/-90, Z 170 to 290). VOLUME and SUB LEVEL legends laser-etched above the two shaft holes.
parts.unknowns: Foam gasket between plate and MDF is needed to keep the upper chamber sealed; not modelled.

parts.name: M4 x 16 countersunk wood screw, black
parts.function: Fixes the control plate to the MDF rear panel at its four corners.
parts.evidence: Brief asks for four M4 corner screws; countersunk so the heads stay flush with the outer face.

parts.name: VOLUME knob, 30 mm aluminium
parts.function: Master volume control for all three amplifier channels.
parts.material: Turned aluminium, 6 mm bore with grub screw
parts.evidence: Brief: 30 mm aluminium knob on the outside. It necessarily protrudes 14 mm beyond the plate outer face (Y 175 to 189), outside the sub-assembly box.

parts.name: SUB LEVEL knob, 30 mm aluminium
parts.function: Sets subwoofer level relative to the upper drivers.
parts.material: Turned aluminium, 6 mm bore with grub screw
parts.evidence: Brief: 30 mm aluminium knob on the amplifier board's sub-level pot shaft. Protrudes 14 mm beyond the plate like the volume knob.

parts.name: 2.1 amplifier board (XH-M139 class)
parts.function: Two TPA3116D2 class-D stages: one in PBTL for the sub, one stereo BTL for channels A and B.
parts.evidence: Brief: about 135 x 85 mm board. Mounted parallel to the plate, component side facing the plate, on 28 mm standoffs so the heatsink clears and the pot shaft reaches through.
parts.unknowns: Actual board outline, hole pattern and pot position vary between sellers; measure the bought board before drilling the plate. The board's other on-board level pots, if present, are left at maximum.

parts.name: M3 x 28 hex standoff
parts.function: Holds the amplifier board 28 mm behind the plate.
parts.evidence: Standoff length chosen from heatsink height (about 21 mm) plus clearance; fixed from outside with M3 countersunk screws.

parts.name: TPA3116D2 (sub channel, PBTL)
parts.function: Class-D output stage in mono PBTL mode driving the 4 ohm subwoofer.
parts.evidence: Brief names TPA3116D2 2.1 board; 2.1 boards of this class use one chip paralleled for the sub.

parts.name: TPA3116D2 (channels A and B, BTL)
parts.function: Stereo class-D output stage for the two full-range channels feeding the crossover.
parts.evidence: Second chip of a 2.1 TPA3116D2 board.

parts.name: Finned aluminium heatsink
parts.function: Spreads heat from both TPA3116D2 chips into the upper chamber air.
parts.evidence: Brief: board with heatsink. Sits on both chips, 6 mm short of the plate.
parts.unknowns: Sealed chamber has no airflow; check heatsink temperature at sustained high level. A thermal pad bridging the 6 mm gap to the plate would help.

parts.name: Output filter inductors
parts.function: LC output filters for the class-D stages (two for the PBTL sub, four for stereo BTL).
parts.evidence: Typical for TPA3116D2 boards: shielded 10 to 22 uH inductors per output leg.

parts.name: Bulk electrolytic capacitors 1000 uF 35 V
parts.function: Supply reservoir for bass peaks on the 24 V rail.
parts.evidence: Typical for this board class; 35 V rating is needed on a 24 V rail.

parts.name: Sub low-pass filter op-amp
parts.function: Buffers the input and low-pass filters it for the subwoofer channel.
parts.evidence: 2.1 boards of this class carry a dual op-amp for the sub filter.
parts.unknowns: Filter corner frequency is fixed by board passives; measure or read values and retune to suit the crossover to the woofer.

parts.name: Sub-level potentiometer on amplifier board
parts.function: Attenuates the filtered signal into the sub amplifier; its shaft passes through the plate.
parts.evidence: Brief: sub-level pot shaft passes through the plate and takes a knob.
parts.unknowns: Shaft length must be at least 25 mm above the board to reach the knob; if the stock pot is shorter, shorten the standoffs or fit a longer-shaft pot.

parts.name: Audio input header, 3 pin
parts.function: Takes the mono signal from the master volume wiper to L, R and sub inputs (L and R bridged).
parts.evidence: Board class has an L/G/R input header; L and R pins are linked so the wiper drives all three inputs.

parts.name: 24 V input screw terminal
parts.function: Receives switched, fused 24 V from the power plate.
parts.evidence: Brief: 24 V input on the amplifier board; sized for 6 A.

parts.name: Sub output screw terminal
parts.function: Speaker output for the subwoofer wire that runs through the shelf pass-through.
parts.evidence: Brief: three screw-terminal speaker outputs.

parts.name: Channel A output screw terminal
parts.function: Speaker output to the crossover woofer input.
parts.evidence: Brief: channel A for the woofer.

parts.name: Channel B output screw terminal
parts.function: Speaker output to the crossover midrange and tweeter input.
parts.evidence: Brief: channel B for midrange and tweeter.

parts.name: Master volume potentiometer 10k log
parts.function: Panel-mounted mono volume control; wiper feeds all three amplifier inputs.
parts.package: 9 mm pot, threaded bushing, 6 mm shaft
parts.evidence: Brief: Alps RK09 class 10k log pot, panel mounted with bushing nut in the plate.

parts.name: Mixer perfboard
parts.function: Carries the L+R summing resistors, the 5 V input, the optional isolator pads and the Bluetooth module socket.
parts.evidence: Brief: small perfboard. Held 62 mm behind the plate so the Bluetooth antenna on it is far from the aluminium.

parts.name: M3 nylon standoff, 62 mm
parts.function: Spaces the mixer board and Bluetooth module well away from the plate.
parts.evidence: Length chosen to place the antenna about 70 mm from the aluminium; can be built from stacked 30 mm spacers.

parts.name: Summing resistors 4.7k
parts.function: Mix left and right line outputs to mono.
parts.evidence: Brief: 2 x 4.7k summing resistors.

parts.name: Optional B0505S isolator position (unpopulated, wire-linked)
parts.function: Pads for an isolated 5 V to 5 V converter in the Bluetooth supply, bridged by two wire links unless hum appears.
parts.evidence: Brief: leave pads for an optional B0505S in case of ground-loop hum.
parts.unknowns: B0505S is limited to 1 W (0.2 A); enough for the receiver, which draws well under 0.1 A. If fitted, remove both links and add 10 uF on its output.

parts.name: 5 V input connector
parts.function: Receives 5 V for the Bluetooth receiver from the power plate's buck converter.
parts.evidence: 5 V up to 0.5 A is provided by the power sub-assembly; a 2-pin keyed connector avoids reversal.

parts.name: Bluetooth module pin header, 6 pin
parts.function: Carries 5 V, ground and stereo line out between the Bluetooth module and the mixer board and supports the module.
parts.evidence: Module class has 2.54 mm pads along one end; a soldered header mounts it 5.8 mm off the perfboard.

parts.name: Bluetooth 5.0 audio receiver board (MH-M28 class)
parts.function: Receives Bluetooth audio and outputs stereo line level.
parts.evidence: Brief: about 35 x 20 mm, 5 V supply. Antenna end overhangs the top of the perfboard, about 70 mm from the plate, radiating through the MDF side and top panels.
parts.unknowns: Pin order differs between module versions; check the silkscreen before wiring.

parts.name: Bluetooth audio SoC
parts.function: Bluetooth radio, decoder and stereo DAC in one chip.
parts.evidence: Modules of this class use a single-chip SoC, often with no usable marking.
parts.unknowns: Read the top mark on the purchased module.

parts.name: PCB trace antenna, 2.4 GHz
parts.function: Meandered inverted-F antenna for Bluetooth.
parts.evidence: Brief: PCB antenna kept clear of the aluminium plate; no copper of the perfboard behind it.
parts.unknowns: Range through 18 mm MDF with a metal plate nearby should be checked; expect about 8 to 10 m.

parts.name: Rear power plate, 2 mm black anodised aluminium
parts.function: Carries the DC jack, fuse holder, rocker switch, power LED and the two small boards, and closes the rear panel opening.
parts.process: Laser cutting or punching, deburr, anodise
parts.evidence: Brief: 220 x 120 mm, 2 mm black aluminium plate with outer face at Y = +175, centred at Z = +80.
parts.unknowns: Hole sizes to match the chosen parts: about 11 mm jack, 12.7 mm fuse holder, 20 mm switch, 8 mm LED bezel, M3 for standoffs. Needs a foam gasket to keep the upper chamber sealed.

parts.name: Plate screw, 4 x 16 mm black pan-head wood screw
parts.function: Clamps the plate and its gasket to the MDF rear panel.
parts.evidence: Brief says the plate is screwed to the rear panel; four corner screws are typical for a plate this size.

parts.name: Panel-mount DC barrel jack, 5.5 x 2.5 mm, high current
parts.function: Accepts the 24 V plug of the external Mean Well GST160A24 adapter.
parts.package: Threaded panel-mount barrel jack with nut
candidates: Generic metal 5.5 x 2.5 mm high-current jack, 8 to 10 A
parts.evidence: Brief asks for a panel-mount 5.5 x 2.5 mm jack rated at least 7 A. The adapter plug mates from outside the plate (Y > 175), outside this box, so it is not modelled.
parts.unknowns: Many 5.5 x 2.5 mm jacks are only rated 5 A. Check the datasheet for at least 7 A, and confirm the GST160A24 plug variant fits (some versions ship with a 4-pin DIN plug instead of a barrel).

parts.name: Panel fuse holder, 5 x 20 mm, with 8 A slow-blow fuse
parts.function: Protects the internal wiring and amplifier against a short on the 24 V line.
parts.package: Screw-cap or bayonet panel holder, 12.7 mm hole
candidates: Fuse: T8A 5 x 20 mm, e.g. Littelfuse 218 series
parts.evidence: Brief: 5 x 20 mm panel fuse holder with an 8 A slow fuse in series with the input.
parts.unknowns: Holder must be rated 10 A; the fuse must have a DC voltage rating of at least 32 V.

parts.name: Round rocker switch, 20 mm, SPST, 10 A DC (KCD1 class)
parts.function: Switches the fused 24 V supply to everything inside the cabinet.
parts.package: Snap-in, 20 mm round hole, 6.3 mm or 4.8 mm tabs
parts.evidence: Brief: round 20 mm rocker rated 10 A DC, in series after the jack.
parts.unknowns: Most KCD1 switches carry an AC rating only. Pick one with a stated DC rating of at least 24 V 10 A, as the 2200 uF inrush is hard on contacts.

parts.name: Green 5 mm power LED in panel bezel
parts.function: Lights when the switched 24 V rail is live.
parts.package: 5 mm through-hole LED in 8 mm bezel
parts.evidence: Brief: green 5 mm power LED in the plate.

parts.name: LED series resistor, 2.2 k, 0.5 W axial, in heat-shrink
parts.function: Limits LED current to about 10 mA from 24 V.
parts.package: Axial, soldered inline on the LED anode lead
parts.evidence: Brief gives 2.2 k; (24 - 2.1) / 2200 is about 10 mA, 0.22 W dissipation, so a 0.5 W part is chosen.

parts.name: 24 V distribution board
parts.function: Takes the switched 24 V, holds the bulk capacitor and breaks out screw terminals for the amplifier and the 5 V feed.
parts.evidence: Designed to give the terminal block and 2200 uF capacitor from the brief a solid mounting; a small single-sided board on standoffs is the simplest way.
parts.unknowns: 24 V pours need to be at least 5 mm wide in 2 oz copper for 6 A. A terminal strip with point-to-point wiring would work equally well.

parts.name: Screw terminal, 2-way, 5.08 mm: 24 V in
parts.function: Lands the red wire from the switch and the black wire from the jack.
parts.evidence: Needed to bring the 16 AWG wires onto the board.

parts.name: Screw terminal, 2-way, 5.08 mm: 24 V out to amplifier
parts.function: Output point for the switched, fused 24 V feed to the TPA3116D2 amplifier board.
parts.evidence: Brief: two-way screw terminal block for the amplifier.

parts.name: Screw terminal, 2-way, 5.08 mm: 5 V out to Bluetooth
parts.function: Output point for the 5 V rail to the Bluetooth receiver board.
parts.evidence: Added so the control plate harness has a defined 5 V pick-up next to the 24 V one.

parts.name: Bulk capacitor, 2200 uF 35 V electrolytic
parts.function: Supplies bass current peaks locally and steadies the 24 V rail behind the long adapter lead.
parts.package: Radial, 16 x 25 mm, 7.5 mm lead pitch
parts.evidence: Brief: 2200 uF 35 V across the 24 V output; 16 x 25 mm is the common can size.
parts.unknowns: Choose a low-ESR 105 C type with ripple rating above 2 A.

parts.name: M3 x 8 mm standoff, distribution board
parts.function: Holds the distribution board 8 mm off the inner face of the plate.
parts.material: Brass, nickel plated, with countersunk M3 screws from the plate face
parts.evidence: Board must clear the plate; two diagonal standoffs suffice for a 60 x 35 mm board.

parts.name: LM2596 buck module board, 43 x 21 mm

unknowns: Every connection is a design assumption; nothing has been built or measured.
The external 24 V adapter has no part id, so its lead to power-dc-jack is not recorded as a connection. A 5.5 x 2.5 mm barrel jack must be a type truly rated for 6 A or more; many are 5 A.

Real output power: on 24 V the sub channel clips near 70 W into 4 ohm and channel A near 30 W into 8 ohm, below the 100 W and 50 W in the brief. The speaker path figures are peaks scaled to fit the 144 W supply.

The 8 A slow-blow fuse sits above the adapter's 6 A limit, so the adapter will current-limit before the fuse opens. The fuse only protects against a fault fed by the charged capacitors or a larger supply. Consider 6.3 A.
Inrush: about 4200 uF (2200 uF on the distribution board plus 2 x 1000 uF on the amplifier) charges through the rocker switch. Whether the adapter hiccups or the switch contacts pit is untested.
Hum from the shared ground between the 5 V buck return and the audio ground: unknown until built. If present, fit the B0505S isolator in the unpopulated pads.

Sub to woofer handover: the woofer section has no high-pass, so the woofer plays everything below 800 Hz and overlaps the sub below 120 Hz. The actual sub low-pass corner of the amplifier board's op-amp filter is not known.
Relative polarity of the sub against the woofer at handover, and of mid and tweeter in the second-order crossover (one is often wired inverted), needs to be set by measurement.
Amplifier heatsink temperature inside a sealed, wadded chamber at sustained high level is not known.
Bluetooth range with the antenna behind an aluminium plate at the rear of the cabinet; MDF passes 2.4 GHz but the plate blocks the rearward direction.
Crossover values are textbook figures for nominal impedances; real driver impedance curves will shift the 800 Hz and 4 kHz points.
Air leakage past the potentiometer shafts, DC jack, switch and fuse holder on the two rear plates.
verifySteps: Before connecting the Bluetooth board, power up and set the buck trimmer so power-term-5v reads 5.0 V; modules often ship set much higher.
Check with a multimeter that no speaker terminal (sub, A or B, + or -) has continuity to ground or to another channel; all outputs are bridged.
Measure the DC voltage at control-amp-dc-term at idle and during loud bass; a sag of more than about 1 V points to thin wiring or the adapter limiting.
Measure idle current on the 24 V line (expect roughly 0.1 A) and the 5 V current to the Bluetooth board (expect under 0.1 A).
Run an impedance sweep at each amplifier output to confirm the load never falls below about 3.2 ohm and to find the port tuning near 45 Hz in the sub trace.
Measure the acoustic response with a microphone near each driver and at 1 m; check the handovers at about 120 Hz, 800 Hz and 4 kHz and try each driver polarity reversed.
With Bluetooth paired and paused, listen for hum or whine at full volume; if present, fit the isolator and repeat.
After 30 minutes of loud music, measure the heatsink temperature through the control plate opening; under about 70 C is comfortable.
Leak test: press the sub cone in gently and release; the woofer cone should not move, and the sub should return slowly only via the port. Do the same on the woofer for the upper chamber.
Walk test for Bluetooth range in front of and behind the cabinet.
safety: Use only an approved, enclosed 24 V adapter; no mains voltage enters the cabinet. Do not exceed 26 V, the TPA3116D2 limit.

The supply capacitors (about 4200 uF at 24 V) stay charged for a while after switch-off and can spark or weld if shorted. Unplug and wait, or discharge through a resistor, before working on the plates.

All speaker outputs are bridged: neither wire is ground. Shorting one to ground or to another channel can destroy the amplifier, and connecting test equipment grounds to them is unsafe for the amplifier.
A short on the 24 V wiring can deliver 6 A continuously below the 8 A fuse rating; use 16 AWG wire, sleeve all terminals and keep wires clear of the heatsink and plate edges.
The heatsink, the 10 W cement resistor on the crossover and the buck inductor get hot; keep wadding and wire insulation away from them.
The cabinet weighs roughly 20 kg and is tall and narrow; fit the feet and keep it on a level floor so it cannot tip.
Cutting and sanding MDF produces fine harmful dust; use extraction and a dust mask.
The 8 inch sub at full level can produce hearing-damaging sound pressure close up; start tests at low volume.

product.name: 4-way Bluetooth tower speaker with 8 inch subwoofer
product.summary: One 18 mm MDF tower, 300 x 350 x 700 mm, with a ported sub chamber of about 26 litres below a fixed shelf and a sealed upper chamber for the woofer, a sealed midrange pocket, the tweeter and the electronics. An external 24 V 6 A desktop adapter feeds a rear barrel jack; a TPA3116D2 2.1 amplifier board drives the sub directly and the upper three drivers through a passive crossover, with a Bluetooth 5.0 receiver board on a 5 V buck rail. It follows the parts blocks in the brief, so it uses an 8 inch sub and a passive crossover; a 10-12 inch sub does not fit the 264 mm internal width and the ADAU1701 DSP is left out. Scale reference: 18 mm MDF panels and the 210 mm frame of the 8 inch driver. Every part is assumed.

unknowns: Every connection is a design assumption; nothing has been built or measured.
The external 24 V adapter has no part id, so its lead to power-dc-jack is not recorded as a connection. A 5.5 x 2.5 mm barrel jack must be a type truly rated for 6 A or more; many are 5 A.

Real output power: on 24 V the sub channel clips near 70 W into 4 ohm and channel A near 30 W into 8 ohm, below the 100 W and 50 W in the brief. The speaker path figures are peaks scaled to fit the 144 W supply.

The 8 A slow-blow fuse sits above the adapter's 6 A limit, so the adapter will current-limit before the fuse opens. The fuse only protects against a fault fed by the charged capacitors or a larger supply. Consider 6.3 A.
Inrush: about 4200 uF (2200 uF on the distribution board plus 2 x 1000 uF on the amplifier) charges through the rocker switch. Whether the adapter hiccups or the switch contacts pit is untested.
Hum from the shared ground between the 5 V buck return and the audio ground: unknown until built. If present, fit the B0505S isolator in the unpopulated pads.

Sub to woofer handover: the woofer section has no high-pass, so the woofer plays everything below 800 Hz and overlaps the sub below 120 Hz. The actual sub low-pass corner of the amplifier board's op-amp filter is not known.
Relative polarity of the sub against the woofer at handover, and of mid and tweeter in the second-order crossover (one is often wired inverted), needs to be set by measurement.
Amplifier heatsink temperature inside a sealed, wadded chamber at sustained high level is not known.
Bluetooth range with the antenna behind an aluminium plate at the rear of the cabinet; MDF passes 2.4 GHz but the plate blocks the rearward direction.
Crossover values are textbook figures for nominal impedances; real driver impedance curves will shift the 800 Hz and 4 kHz points.
Air leakage past the potentiometer shafts, DC jack, switch and fuse holder on the two rear plates.
verifySteps: Before connecting the Bluetooth board, power up and set the buck trimmer so power-term-5v reads 5.0 V; modules often ship set much higher.
Check with a multimeter that no speaker terminal (sub, A or B, + or -) has continuity to ground or to another channel; all outputs are bridged.
Measure the DC voltage at control-amp-dc-term at idle and during loud bass; a sag of more than about 1 V points to thin wiring or the adapter limiting.
Measure idle current on the 24 V line (expect roughly 0.1 A) and the 5 V current to the Bluetooth board (expect under 0.1 A).
Run an impedance sweep at each amplifier output to confirm the load never falls below about 3.2 ohm and to find the port tuning near 45 Hz in the sub trace.
Measure the acoustic response with a microphone near each driver and at 1 m; check the handovers at about 120 Hz, 800 Hz and 4 kHz and try each driver polarity reversed.
With Bluetooth paired and paused, listen for hum or whine at full volume; if present, fit the isolator and repeat.
After 30 minutes of loud music, measure the heatsink temperature through the control plate opening; under about 70 C is comfortable.
Leak test: press the sub cone in gently and release; the woofer cone should not move, and the sub should return slowly only via the port. Do the same on the woofer for the upper chamber.
Walk test for Bluetooth range in front of and behind the cabinet.
safety: Use only an approved, enclosed 24 V adapter; no mains voltage enters the cabinet. Do not exceed 26 V, the TPA3116D2 limit.

The supply capacitors (about 4200 uF at 24 V) stay charged for a while after switch-off and can spark or weld if shorted. Unplug and wait, or discharge through a resistor, before working on the plates.

All speaker outputs are bridged: neither wire is ground. Shorting one to ground or to another channel can destroy the amplifier, and connecting test equipment grounds to them is unsafe for the amplifier.
A short on the 24 V wiring can deliver 6 A continuously below the 8 A fuse rating; use 16 AWG wire, sleeve all terminals and keep wires clear of the heatsink and plate edges.
The heatsink, the 10 W cement resistor on the crossover and the buck inductor get hot; keep wadding and wire insulation away from them.
The cabinet weighs roughly 20 kg and is tall and narrow; fit the feet and keep it on a level floor so it cannot tip.
Cutting and sanding MDF produces fine harmful dust; use extraction and a dust mask.
The 8 inch sub at full level can produce hearing-damaging sound pressure close up; start tests at low volume.
